jonkershoek.name: Jonkershoek
jonkershoek.difficulty: Green: 1 trail, Blue: 5 trails, Red: 6 trails, Black: 6 trails
jonkershoek.permit: R90 MTB · R80 runners & hikers · R70 students. Pay by card at the gate or in advance on the MTO App. No booking required, just pitch up.
jonkershoek.getting_there: Coordinates: 33°57'48.70"S 18°55'31.98"E. From Cape Town take the N2 towards Stellenbosch. Take exit 33 for Baden Powell Drive (R310). Approach Stellenbosch on the R310, turn left on the R44 then right into Merriman Avenue. Continue straight at the traffic circle onto Jonkershoek Road and follow it all the way to the MTO Forestry gate.
jonkershoek.seasons: Winter is when Jonkershoek shines, the trails drain exceptionally well after rain and the mountain scenery is at its most dramatic. Summer can be dry and dusty. The South Easter howls on the ridges in summer so ride early mornings. Always check the Jonkershoek social pages for trail closure notices during the rainy season.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride Jonkershoek?
faqs.a: Jonkershoek is not recommended for beginners. The trails are long, technical and involve serious climbing. Get a few other Western Cape trails under your belt first — Bloemendal, Hillcrest or the Greenbelts are great starting points.

faqs.q: How much is the Jonkershoek permit?
faqs.a: R90 for MTB, R80 for runners and hikers, R70 for students. Pay by card at the gate or in advance on the MTO App. No booking required.

faqs.q: Where do I park at Jonkershoek?
faqs.a: Park at the CapeNature Jonkershoek Entrance off Jonkershoek Road, just outside Stellenbosch. The parking area is safe and well-managed. Arrive early on weekends — it fills up fast.

faqs.q: What is the best trail at Jonkershoek?
faqs.a: The Armageddon Trail is the standout. It traverses 8 levels and has the biggest variety of trail features of any single trail at Jonkershoek — it could well be one of the best trails in the country.

faqs.q: What is the best season to ride Jonkershoek?
faqs.a: Winter. The trails drain exceptionally well and the mountain scenery is at its most dramatic. Avoid summer afternoons when the South Easter howls on the exposed ridges. Ride early mornings in summer.

faqs.q: Is there coffee or food at Jonkershoek?
faqs.a: Yes — Balance Coffee at the Jonkershoek entrance has a coffee shot, limited food and drinks and free wifi. Perfect for a pre or post-ride stop. Stellenbosch town is also just a short drive away for more options.

faqs.q: Can I take my kids to Jonkershoek?
faqs.a: Not ideal for young or beginner kids. The trails are demanding and long. Kids with solid MTB skills and good fitness can enjoy it but it is not a family beginner destination.

faqs.q: Are dogs allowed at Jonkershoek?
faqs.a: Dogs are not permitted in the Jonkershoek Nature Reserve.

local_knowledge: The permit gate opens at 07h00 on weekends in summer and 8am in winter — arrive 30 min before to beat the queue, especially in summer when the car park fills by 7am.
Cell signal disappears completely once you drop into the valley past the first stream crossing. Download your map or GPX before you leave the gate.
The Armageddon Trail runs east to west — ride it in the morning when the sun is behind you. Afternoon light directly into your eyes on the descent is not fun.

tokai.name: Tokai MTB
tokai.difficulty: Green: 2 trails, Blue: 10 trails, Black: 10 trails
tokai.permit: R100 per day or purchase an annual activity permit. Details available at the trailheads. Hiking is also permitted on the network.
tokai.getting_there: Parking available at the Silvermine Entrance or the lower Tokai Forest, both free and safe. From Cape Town take the M3 south, exit at Tokai Road and turn right. Follow signs to the Tokai Forest or Silvermine. Facilities including toilets are available at the trailhead.
tokai.seasons: Tokai rides well in both summer and winter. Summer is dry and loose, rocky and technical, so ride with confidence. Winter turns the trails wet and grippy and the reserve looks incredible in the rain. Trails generally stay open but use common sense after heavy rain and keep an eye on their social media for any announcements. Take plenty of water in summer, once you are in the reserve it can get hot.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride Tokai MTB?
faqs.a: Tokai has something for everyone but is primarily a climbing and descending trail. Beginners can access the lower forest tracks but the main MTB trails are intermediate to advanced. Start on the easier forest roads first.

faqs.q: How much is the Tokai MTB permit?
faqs.a: R100 per day. Annual activity permits are also available. Details at the trailhead. Hiking is also permitted on the same permit.

faqs.q: Where do I park at Tokai?
faqs.a: Park at the Silvermine Entrance or the lower Tokai Forest parking area — both are free and safe. From Cape Town take the M3 south towards Muizenberg, exit at Tokai Road and follow the signs.

faqs.q: What is the best season to ride Tokai?
faqs.a: Tokai rides well year-round. Summer is dry and dusty with faster, looser trails. Winter brings moisture, better grip and lush surroundings. Ride mornings in both seasons.

faqs.q: Is there coffee or food at Tokai?
faqs.a: No cafe at the trailhead. Constantia is a short drive away with excellent restaurants and coffee.

faqs.q: Are dogs allowed at Tokai?
faqs.a: Dogs are permitted on leads in certain sections of the Tokai Forest. Check current regulations at the gate as rules can vary by area.

local_knowledge: The best parking is at the lower Tokai Forest entrance off Tokai Road, not the Silvertree Restaurant entrance — the latter gets congested and the restaurant parking is not always open.
Tokai is pretty much an up and down trail. Loads of climbing and then a descent to the gate. Make sure you are ready for that — it can get really hot and tiring in summer.

After heavy rain, the clay sections get slippery and there is a lot of pooled water on the jeep tracks. The trails hold up better than most in the wet but always check the Tokai MTB trail website for closures.

bloemendal.name: Bloemendal
bloemendal.difficulty: Green: 3 trails, Blue: 4 trails, Black: 1 trail
bloemendal.permit: R75 MTB · R40 runners. Permits available at the kiosk on arrival or online. For function bookings contact Bloemendal Wine Estate directly.
bloemendal.getting_there: From Durbanville: Turn left off the M13 into the Bloemendal Wine Estate. Drive past the Bon Amis Restaurant on your left. Turn right at the Bike Park Parking, Bloemendal Trail Park will be on your right. From Blouberg: Turn right off the M13 into Bloemendal Wine Estate. Drive past the Bon Amis Restaurant on your left. Turn right at the Bike Park Parking. Loads of safe parking available on site.
bloemendal.seasons: Bloemendal rides well in all seasons. The farm is part of the Tygerberg Trail Network and gets muddy in the rainy winter months, trails may close after heavy rain. All closure notices are posted on their website and social media pages. Summer riding is fast and fun.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride Bloemendal?
faqs.a: Absolutely — Bloemendal is one of the best beginner MTB destinations in the Western Cape. The trails are smooth, well-signed and forgiving. If you just bought your first MTB, start here.

faqs.q: How much is the Bloemendal permit?
faqs.a: R75 for MTB, R40 for runners. Permits available at the kiosk on arrival or online.

faqs.q: Where do I park at Bloemendal?
faqs.a: Turn left off the M13 into Bloemendal Wine Estate, Durbanville. Drive past the Bon Amis Restaurant and follow signs to the trail parking. Safe, shaded and well-maintained.

faqs.q: Is Bloemendal good for families?
faqs.a: Yes — one of the best family MTB destinations in the Cape. The trails are flat to gently rolling, well-marked and suitable for kids who can ride confidently.

faqs.q: Is there coffee or food at Bloemendal?
faqs.a: Yes — the Bon Amis Restaurant on the estate is excellent for post-ride food and coffee. One of the best post-ride stops in the Western Cape.

faqs.q: What is the best season to ride Bloemendal?
faqs.a: Year-round. The farm drains reasonably well in winter. Summer riding on the vineyard paths in the late afternoon is particularly beautiful.

local_knowledge: The Trail Hub kitchen closes at 17h00 on weekdays — if you want a proper post-ride meal, plan to be off the trails by 16h30.
The B-Spot trail on the left as you cycle towards the vineyard climb is the best warm-up. Five minutes on this trail and your legs are ready.
Beginners can start on the Bloemenice trail as well as the flow line. If you want to really test your skill, head to Bloemendaaler on the Upper Bloemendal trails for a proper rush.

hillcrest.name: Hillcrest
hillcrest.permit: R75 permit available on the estate or through the Tygerberg MTB Club. Restaurant bookings should be made directly with Hillcrest Estate.
hillcrest.getting_there: From Cape Town take the N1 north, exit onto the M56 (Tygerberg Valley Road) and turn onto Contermanskloof Road following signs for the Durbanville Wine Valley. Loads of safe parking available on the estate. Use Waze for the most up to date directions.
hillcrest.seasons: Hillcrest rides well all year round. Trails are fast and fun in summer and drain well in winter. Keep an eye on the Tygerberg MTB Club social pages before and after heavy rain for any trail closure notices.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride Hillcrest?
faqs.a: Hillcrest has beginner-friendly options but also more challenging trails. First-timers should start on the easier green routes and build from there.

faqs.q: Where do I park at Hillcrest?
faqs.a: Hillcrest Estate is in the Tygerberg Hills just outside Durbanville, about 30 minutes from Cape Town. Follow signs to Hillcrest Estate off the R304.

faqs.q: Is there coffee or food at Hillcrest?
faqs.a: Yes — Hillcrest Estate has a restaurant and tasting room. Post-ride wine tasting with ocean views is one of the genuine highlights of this destination.

faqs.q: What is the best trail at Hillcrest?
faqs.a: The trails with ocean views towards Table Bay are the standout experience. On a clear day the views are among the best you will find anywhere in the Western Cape.

faqs.q: Is Hillcrest good for families?
faqs.a: Yes — suitable trails for family riders with some experience. The estate setting is beautiful and the post-ride facilities make it a great day out.

local_knowledge: The ocean views towards Table Bay are best on clear winter mornings after rain has washed the atmosphere — visibility can stretch all the way to Robben Island.
Weekday mornings are significantly quieter than weekends. Tuesday and Wednesday tend to be the emptiest days on the trails.
The tasting room at Hillcrest Estate serves food until 15h00. The wine list is excellent and the estate produces some underrated red blends worth trying post-ride.

contermanskloof.name: Contermanskloof
contermanskloof.difficulty: Green: 1 trail, Blue: 3 trails, Black: 7 trails
contermanskloof.permit: R75 permit available at the Dairy Shed, or via Snapscan or Zapper at the trail kiosk. Book a table at Starke Brews separately, it is very popular.
contermanskloof.getting_there: GPS: -33.7812, 18.6234. From Cape Town take the N1 north, exit at Durbanville / Contermanskloof Road. Follow Contermanskloof Road past the wine farms to the trailhead. Loads of parking at the farm.
contermanskloof.seasons: Contermanskloof rides brilliantly all year round, some of the best riding you will ever do in both summer and winter. Trails drain well but it is never a good idea to ride after heavy rain. Keep an eye on the Tygerberg MTB Club website and Contermanskloof social pages for any closure notices.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride Contermanskloof?
faqs.a: Contermanskloof has beginner options but the network is large and confusing on your first visit. Go with someone who knows the trails.

faqs.q: Where do I park at Contermanskloof?
faqs.a: GPS coordinates: -33.802997, 18.589407. Follow the main entrance road to the designated trail parking area.

faqs.q: What makes Contermanskloof special?
faqs.a: Once you know your way around, Contermanskloof is one of the most exciting trail networks in the Cape. The variety is exceptional — from flowy singletrack to technical descents.

faqs.q: What is the best season to ride Contermanskloof?
faqs.a: Summer is the prime season when trails are dry and fast. Winter can get muddy in places but the network is large enough that you can always find good riding.

faqs.q: Is Contermanskloof good for families?
faqs.a: With the right trail selection, yes. There are easier routes suitable for families but the network size means navigation experience helps.

faqs.q: Is there coffee or food at Contermanskloof?
faqs.a: Two great options on site. The Dairy Shed does excellent coffee and is famous for the best carrot cake around — they also do breakfasts. Starke Brews is a world-class brewery run by trail builder Rob Starke, with a great selection of craft beers, pizza and a kids play area. One of the best post-ride setups of any hub in the Western Cape.

local_knowledge: First-timers should screenshot the trail map before entering the network. The signage is good but the sheer number of intersections makes it easy to go in circles on your first visit.
Starke Brews is the best post-ride stop in the Durbanville network, period. Rob Starke built most of these trails and his IPA is exceptional. The pizza is worth the wait.
The South Easter adds 15-20km/h to your speed on the exposed ridgeline sections heading west — great for PBs in summer on the Rhinos and Happy Hops.

meerendal.name: Meerendal MTB
meerendal.difficulty: Green: 3 trails, Blue: 5 trails, Black: 2 trails
meerendal.permit: Trail pass required. Book and pay online via the Meerendal Wine Estate website. Walk-in available but book ahead for weekends.
meerendal.getting_there: From Cape Town take the N1 north, exit at Durbanville. Follow signs to Meerendal Wine Estate on Vissershok Road.
meerendal.seasons: Rideable year-round. Avoid vine block sections during harvest (February–April) when workers are active. Winter mornings are exceptional.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride Meerendal?
faqs.a: Meerendal is an intermediate to advanced destination. The climbing is serious and the trails demand fitness and skill. Build up at Bloemendal or Hillcrest first.

faqs.q: What makes Meerendal famous?
faqs.a: Meerendal hosted the Cape Epic Prologue — one of the most celebrated MTB events in the world. The trails that hosted that race are available for public riding.

faqs.q: Is there coffee or food at Meerendal?
faqs.a: Yes — Meerendal has an excellent restaurant and tasting room on the estate. Post-ride wine tasting here is a real highlight.

faqs.q: What is the best season to ride Meerendal?
faqs.a: Year-round. The estate trails drain well and the views across the Durbanville Hills are spectacular in all seasons.

local_knowledge: If you want to see the proper Meerendal, pack your legs and head up to the top of Dorstberg. The descent will blow your mind — it's fast and narrow, so experienced riders only.
Meerendal Estate wines are seriously good and the tasting room is one of the nicer estate facilities in Durbanville. Book ahead on weekends as it gets busy.
The trails closest to the estate buildings tend to be the most technical, but the outer loops are more forgiving and better suited to building into the network on your first visit.

majik.name: Majik Forest
majik.difficulty: Green: 2 trails, Blue: 4 trails, Black: 2 trails
majik.permit: Free to ride. Multi-use public trails no permit required. Park at Bloemendal Wine Estate or along the access road.
majik.getting_there: From Cape Town take the N1 north, exit at Durbanville. Head to Bloemendal Wine Estate on Bottelary Road Majik Forest sits directly behind the farm.
majik.seasons: Good year-round. Trails are raw and natural so conditions vary after rain. Quieter on weekday mornings busiest on weekend mornings with runners and dog walkers.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride Majik Forest?
faqs.a: Yes — Majik Forest is one of the more accessible trail areas in the Durbanville network. The natural multi-use trails welcome everyone from beginners to seasoned riders.

faqs.q: Where do I park at Majik Forest?
faqs.a: Majik Forest is behind Bloemendal Wine Farm in Durbanville. Access via the Bloemendal Estate or the dedicated Majik Forest entrance.

faqs.q: What is Majik Forest like to ride?
faqs.a: Raw and natural. These are multi-use trails through indigenous forest and fynbos — not manicured singletrack. Expect roots, rocks and a more adventurous feel.

faqs.q: Is there coffee at Majik Forest?
faqs.a: No dedicated cafe on site. Bloemendal Wine Estate and Durbanville village are close by.

local_knowledge: Majik Forest is a shared-use area with trail runners and hikers. Please yield to pedestrians on the narrow singletrack and announce yourself on blind corners.
The forest floor sections stay damp long after rain, making Majik one of the slippier wet-weather options in the Durbanville network due to the number of roots under the canopy.
The connection through to Bloemendal Wine Estate is worth exploring — riding both in a single session makes for a satisfying 2-3 hour loop. Just make sure you buy your permit!

cbd.name: Cape Town CBD Trails
cbd.region: Table Mountain · Signal Hill · Cape Town
cbd.difficulty: Green: 1 trail, Blue: 2 trails, Red: 1 trail, Black: 1 trail
cbd.permit: SANParks activity permit required. Day permit approximately R50 to R100, annual activity permit around R700 to R800. Buy online via the SANParks website or at SANParks offices and gates. No booking required. Carry your permit while riding. Some connected areas may require a CapeNature permit.
cbd.getting_there: GPS: -33.94, 18.41. Main access points are the Signal Hill parking area off Signal Hill Road, Kloof Nek (most central), and De Waal Park. From the city centre follow Buitenkant Street to De Waal Drive or take Kloof Street up to Kloof Nek. Go early, parking fills and security is better in the morning. Do not leave valuables in your car.
cbd.seasons: Year-round riding but the South Easter wind from October to March is a major factor on the exposed ridges. Autumn and spring are the best balance of conditions. Trails are fully natural with no formal closure system, rideable year-round but rocky sections become more dangerous after rain. Early mornings are best in every season.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride the Cape Town CBD Trails?
faqs.a: Not recommended for beginners. The terrain is raw, steep and unforgiving. These are serious mountain trails directly above the city. Build experience elsewhere first.

faqs.q: What makes the Cape Town CBD trails unique?
faqs.a: You are riding raw mountain terrain directly above one of the most beautiful cities on earth. The views of the city, harbour and Atlantic Ocean mid-ride are unlike anything else in South African MTB.

faqs.q: What is the best season for Cape Town CBD trails?
faqs.a: Dry summer months are best. Winter rain can make the mountain trails extremely slippery and dangerous. Always check conditions before heading up.

faqs.q: Are the CBD trails technical?
faqs.a: Very. These are serious mountain trails with exposed sections, loose rock and significant technical challenge. Fitness and skill are both required.

local_knowledge: Pat's Track descent is the must-do line. Access from the top via De Waal Drive parking and descend toward the city — the views mid-descent are genuinely extraordinary.
Signal Hill is an undiscovered gem — it would be our first stop when riding in town, followed by the rock slabs on Table Mountain.
The loose rocky sections on Table Mountain contour paths require real technical skill in the wet. If it rained in the last 48 hours, stick to Signal Hill where the paths drain faster.

hoogekraal.name: Hoogekraal Farm
hoogekraal.difficulty: Green: 3 trails, Blue: 4 trails, Black: 1 trail
hoogekraal.permit: R75 day permit, or a valid Tygerberg MTB Club membership. Pay at the trailhead. No booking required.
hoogekraal.getting_there: From Cape Town take the N1 north, exit at Durbanville. Follow the Durbanville Hills road toward Hoogekraal Farm easily combined with Contermanskloof and Fair Cape in one day.
hoogekraal.seasons: Good year-round. Part of the Tygerberg Network so conditions are similar to Contermanskloof and Bloemendal. Check local social media after heavy rain.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride Hoogekraal?
faqs.a: Hoogekraal is accessible to riders with some experience. The trails are not overly technical but require basic MTB skills. A good step up from Bloemendal.

faqs.q: How much is the Hoogekraal permit?
faqs.a: R75 day permit or a valid Tygerberg MTB Club membership. Pay at the trailhead. No booking required.

faqs.q: What are the best trails at Hoogekraal?
faqs.a: The Cobra trail and Snake Rattle and Roll are the highlights — flowing, fun singletrack that makes the most of the Durbanville Hills terrain.

faqs.q: Is there coffee at Hoogekraal?
faqs.a: Yes — Hoogekraal has a newly opened cafe on site serving coffee and basic snacks. A welcome stop before or after your ride.

local_knowledge: The newly opened cafe at the trailhead is cash-friendly but card is preferred. Bring both on your first visit until you know what they accept.
Snake Rattle and Roll is the trail locals come back to repeatedly. It's flowing, technical enough to keep you honest and perfectly paced. Ride it twice if you have the legs.
The Tygerberg MTB Club membership pays for itself quickly if you plan to ride the Durbanville network more than a few times a season, as it covers Hoogekraal, Fair Cape and several other farms.

greenbelts.name: Green Belts
greenbelts.difficulty: Green: 3 trails, Blue: 2 trails, Red: 1 trail, Black: 0 trails
greenbelts.permit: No permit required. Completely free, open public space managed by the city. No SANParks permit needed unless you ride into the Table Mountain trails proper. No booking, no indemnity, just ride.
greenbelts.getting_there: GPS: -34.02, 18.42. Main access points are the Alphen Trail (easiest and safest start), Constantia Village Shopping Centre and the Klaasenbosch Trailhead. Alphen is the recommended first stop. Park in visible areas and do not leave valuables in your car.
greenbelts.seasons: Year-round riding. Summer is excellent thanks to the shade from mature trees, rare in Cape Town riding. Winter is still rideable with some muddy patches and puddles along river sections after rain. The greenbelts drain better than mountain trails and are generally more forgiving in all conditions. Mornings and late afternoons are the best times.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride the Constantia Greenbelts?
faqs.a: Yes — the Greenbelts are one of the most accessible MTB routes in Cape Town. Shaded, flat to gently rolling and well-connected. Perfect for beginners, families and relaxed riding.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to ride the Greenbelts?
faqs.a: The Constantia Greenbelts are free to access. No permit required.

faqs.q: Are the Greenbelts good for families?
faqs.a: Excellent for families. The shaded forest paths and gentle terrain make this one of the most family-friendly riding areas in the Cape.

faqs.q: How long are the Greenbelt trails?
faqs.a: The network links Constantia, Tokai and Kirstenbosch. You can ride anywhere from 10km to 30km+ depending on your route.

faqs.q: Is there coffee near the Greenbelts?
faqs.a: Yes — Constantia Village, Kirstenbosch and the Constantia wine estates are all close by.

local_knowledge: The Cecilia Forest entrance on Rhodes Drive is the best starting point for connecting Constantia to Kirstenbosch — it puts you right in the middle of the network with options in both directions.
The Greenbelts are popular with dog walkers, especially on weekend mornings. Bell or call out on blind corners and keep speed manageable through the shared sections.

Kirstenbosch Gardens charges an entry fee if you enter via the main gate. The MTB connection through the back of the garden is informal and usually open but ask locals for the current preferred entry point.

stbfund.name: Stellenbosch Trail Fund
stbfund.difficulty: Green: 3 trails, Blue: 6 trails, Red: 5 trails, Black: 2 trails
stbfund.permit: Free to ride, no permit required. Donations are encouraged via SnapScan and Zapper donation points on the trails. If you plan to link into Jonkershoek, Banhoek or Bottelary you will need the Winelands annual permit at around R1800.
stbfund.getting_there: Multiple entry points into the network. Coetzenburg Stadium is the easiest and most central starting point. Eden Forest is quieter and great for forest riding. Mont Marie Restaurant gives you trail access plus a coffee stop. Botmaskop is the choice for proper climbing and descents. From Cape Town take the N1 or R44 into Stellenbosch and head toward Coetzenburg or Eden depending on your route. Always lock valuables in your car.
stbfund.seasons: Year-round riding with autumn, spring and winter being the standout seasons. Winter brings cool temperatures and hero dirt, the forest sections ride brilliantly after rain. Some trails can get slippery and muddy after heavy rain and may be avoided to prevent damage. Check STF social media before heading out if it has rained.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to ride the Stellenbosch Trail Fund trails?
faqs.a: The Stellenbosch Trail Fund trails are free to ride. The Fund is supported by voluntary contributions.

faqs.q: Where do I park for the Stellenbosch Trail Fund?
faqs.a: Multiple trailheads exist around Stellenbosch town. The Idas Valley and Jonkershoek Valley entrances are popular.

faqs.q: What makes the Stellenbosch Trail Fund special?
faqs.a: 50km+ of trails through a university town, entirely free. Maintained by volunteers and community support. The variety of terrain around Stellenbosch is exceptional.

faqs.q: Is there coffee near the STF trails?
faqs.a: Stellenbosch town is one of the best post-ride destinations in South Africa — excellent coffee, restaurants, wine farms and vibrant atmosphere.

local_knowledge: The Idas Valley trailhead has limited parking but no permit fee. Arrive before 08h00 on weekends to get a spot — the Jonkershoek Valley entrance has more parking.
The STF network links directly into the Jonkershoek reserve at certain points. Clarify where the free STF trails end and the CapeNature permit zone begins before you ride into the reserve.
Stellenbosch has some of the best post-ride coffee in the Western Cape. Schoon de Companje on Church Street is a local favourite — arrive before 10h00 on weekends to avoid the queue.

helderberg.name: Helderberg Farm
helderberg.difficulty: Green: 1 trail, Blue: 1 trail, Red: 1 trail, Black: 1 trail
helderberg.permit: R100 adults, R50 kids. Pay at the kiosk or Tea Garden on site, or via The Hanger Bike Co. No booking required but permits are mandatory, no permit, no ride. An annual permit is available at around R500–R650 and is also covered by the Winelands annual pass.
helderberg.getting_there: GPS: -34.02, 18.86. From Cape Town take the N2 toward Somerset West, then the R44 toward Stellenbosch. Turn onto Klein Helderberg Road and follow signs to Helderberg Farm. Safe parking at the main farm area, arrive early on weekends as it gets busy.
helderberg.seasons: Autumn through spring is best, the trails ride beautifully when temperatures are cooler. Summer is hot and exposed on the climbs so early morning starts are essential. Trails may close after heavy rain as they can get loose and rutted. Always check their social media for trail status before heading out.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride Helderberg Farm?
faqs.a: Helderberg has something for all levels. Beginners should start on the easier routes and build up to the flow and downhill sections.

faqs.q: What makes Helderberg unique?
faqs.a: One of the few places in the Western Cape where you can ride XC, flow trail and downhill in a single session. Rare variety of disciplines in one location.

faqs.q: Is there coffee at Helderberg Farm?
faqs.a: Yes — Helderberg Farm has a restaurant on site.

faqs.q: What is the best season for Helderberg?
faqs.a: Year-round. The Helderberg Basin can offer good riding even when the Cape is wet.

local_knowledge: The downhill trail at Helderberg is gravity-only and runs top to bottom — there is no looping back up on the DH line itself. Riders typically shuttle with vehicles or combine with the XC climb.
Somerset West is significantly warmer than Cape Town in winter. Helderberg is a reliable option when the Cape gets cold and wet, often with bluebird conditions while the Peninsula is grey.
The restaurant on site does a solid breakfast. Getting there before 09h00 on weekends means you can eat, ride and be back for a late lunch while most people are still arriving.

bottlery.name: Bottelary Hills
bottlery.difficulty: Green: 2 trails, Blue: 2 trails, Red: 1 trail, Black: 0 trails
bottlery.permit: R100 day permit, R1050 annual. Available at wine farms including Jordan, Hazendal and Zevenwacht, at Engen Soneike and Shell Kruispad petrol stations, and at some 24-hour security gates. Mostly cashless via Zapper. No booking required but you must display your permit board on your bike.
bottlery.getting_there: No single trailhead, you choose your start point. Jordan Wine Estate, Hazendal, Zevenwacht, Devonvale and Asara are all popular. From Cape Town take the N1 and access via Bottelary Road (M23) or Devon Valley Road on the Stellenbosch side. Park only at designated farm access points and do not leave valuables in your car.
bottlery.seasons: Year-round riding with autumn and spring being best. Summer is very hot with minimal shade so start early and bring more water than you think you need. After rain the jeep tracks get sticky and muddy but the network is usually still rideable. Wind picks up later in the day, get out early.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride Bottelary Hills?
faqs.a: Suitable for riders with basic fitness and skill. Open rolling farmland rather than technical mountain trails — accessible to a wide range of riders.

faqs.q: What is Bottelary Hills like to ride?
faqs.a: Classic country riding across 20+ working wine farms. Open, scenic and fitness-focused with 70 to 120km of trail. More pastoral and relaxed than the mountain trails closer to Cape Town.

faqs.q: What is the best season for Bottelary Hills?
faqs.a: Spring and autumn are beautiful. Summer can be hot so start early. Winter is generally fine but some sections can get muddy.

local_knowledge: The Bottelary network crosses active wine farm land. Stick to marked trails and respect farm operations, especially during harvest from February to April when vehicles and equipment are everywhere.
Navigation requires a downloaded map or GPX. The trail signage across the farms is inconsistent and some junctions are unmarked — Trailforks with offline maps is essential.

The best riding in Bottelary is the exposed ridgeline sections with views across both the Cape Winelands and Table Mountain. These sections get hot in summer — start early and carry more water than you think you need.

banhoek.name: Banhoek
banhoek.difficulty: Green: 1 trail, Blue: 2 trails, Red: 3 trails, Black: 0 trails
banhoek.permit: R100 day permit. Buy online via SnapScan or Zapper QR codes at the access points, pay and keep proof on your phone. No booking required, just arrive and ride. A Winelands Regional Permit also gives access to Banhoek alongside Paarl Trails, Franschhoek Trails and Wellington Trails, over 1000km of combined riding on one permit.
banhoek.getting_there: GPS: -33.9167, 18.9667 (Old Bethlehem Gate). From Stellenbosch take the Helshoogte Pass (R310) toward Franschhoek and turn into the Kylemore and Banhoek Valley. Multiple access points including Banhoek Chilli Oil, Bethlehem Farm, Bartinney Wine Estate, Boschendal and the Banhoek Farm Store, the flexible entry points make ride planning very easy.
banhoek.seasons: Autumn is the sweet spot, cool temperatures, firm trails and incredible valley colours. Spring is lush and flowing. Summer gets hot on the exposed climbs so start early. After rain the river crossings and some soil sections get soft and technical descents become slippery, ride responsibly and stay on marked routes.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride Banhoek?
faqs.a: Banhoek is primarily intermediate to advanced. The climbing is significant and technical sections demand skill. Intermediate riders will find it challenging and rewarding — beginners should build up elsewhere first.

faqs.q: Where do I park at Banhoek?
faqs.a: Banhoek Valley is accessed from the R310 between Stellenbosch and Franschhoek. Park at the Old Bethlehem Farm trailhead.

faqs.q: What makes Banhoek one of the best trails in the Western Cape?
faqs.a: The singletrack at Banhoek is among the most perfectly built in the country. Tight, flowing, technically interesting and set in one of the most beautiful valleys in the Western Cape.

faqs.q: Is there coffee at Banhoek?
faqs.a: Babylonstoren, La Motte and the Franschhoek restaurant mile are all within easy reach post-ride.

faqs.q: What is the best season for Banhoek?
faqs.a: Spring and autumn are spectacular. Summer is hot so ride early mornings. Winter trails are lush and the mountains are dramatic.

local_knowledge: The Banhoek Valley gets significantly hotter than Stellenbosch town in summer. Start before 08h00 in December and January — by 10h30 the valley is baking and the climbing is brutal in the heat.
Boschendal farm shop and deli is 10 minutes from the trailhead and is one of the finest post-ride stops in South Africa. Go for the deli rather than the restaurant if you want to eat quickly.

The singletrack at Banhoek is tight and technical in places. Riders who are comfortable at intermediate level will find it demands more than it looks on paper. But at the end of the day, some of the best singletrack you will ever ride in your life.

dornier.name: Dornier
dornier.difficulty: Blue: 1 trail, Red: 1 trail, Black: 0 trails, Green: 0 trails
dornier.permit: R60–R100 day permit via the Wine Lands Cycling Club platform or partner outlets. Important, day permits may not be sold at the cellar door itself so buy in advance online. A Wine Lands Regional permit gives broad access to Dornier, Spier, Helderberg Farm, Stellenzicht and more. No booking required, just carry and display your permit while riding.
dornier.getting_there: GPS: -34.0534, 18.8647. From Cape Town take the N2 or R44 toward Stellenbosch, then turn toward Upper Blaauwklippen Road and follow signs to Dornier Wine Estate. Farm parking is right at the estate near the tasting room, safe, visible and easy to find.
dornier.seasons: Autumn through spring is most pleasant with firmer ground and cooler temperatures. Summer is rideable but bring extra water as it gets warm. After prolonged rain some sections become slick and muddy, the trail generally handles light rain well but check conditions before heading out.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride Dornier?
faqs.a: Yes — the Dornier Loop is a scenic, shorter ride through forest and vineyard that suits a wide range of riders.

faqs.q: Is there food and wine at Dornier?
faqs.a: Yes — the Dornier restaurant is excellent. The trail starts and ends at the winery making a ride and tasting a natural combination.

faqs.q: What is the Dornier Loop like?
faqs.a: A scenic 10-12km singletrack loop through forest and vineyard with a winery finish. Not technically demanding but beautiful throughout.

faqs.q: What is the best season for Dornier?
faqs.a: Year-round. The shaded forest sections ride well even in summer heat. Autumn is particularly beautiful.

local_knowledge: The Dornier loop is a single direction trail — follow the arrows. Riders going the wrong way create dangerous blind-corner situations on a route with no room to pass.
The Dornier restaurant serves one of the better winery lunches in the Helderberg area. Make a booking if you are going on a weekend as the terrace fills up fast, especially in spring.

The trail passes through beautiful old oak forest in the lower sections. These trees were planted in the early 1900s and the canopy is genuinely impressive. Slow down and take it in rather than just blasting through.

muratie.name: Muratie MTB
muratie.difficulty: Green: 1 trail, Blue: 3 trails, Red: 1 trail, Black: 0 trails
muratie.permit: R100 day permit. Buy at the Dirtopia Trail Centre on site opposite the wine cellar, or online via Dirtpass with Snapscan and Zapper options available. No booking required for daily entry but an indemnity form must be completed. If you need a bike rental, book at least 24 hours in advance.
muratie.getting_there: From Cape Town take the N1 east to Stellenbosch, then head toward the R44 and turn onto Knorhoek Road. Muratie is clearly signposted on Knorhoek Road just outside town. Note that GPS can be imprecise once you are on Knorhoek Road follow the estate signage. Parking is at the cellar and Trail Centre.
muratie.seasons: Autumn through spring is ideal with cooler temperatures and firmer trails. Summer is manageable thanks to shaded forest sections but bring extra water. After light rain the trails are generally still rideable. Steep sections can get slick after heavy rain so check conditions before heading out.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride Muratie MTB?
faqs.a: Muratie has trails suitable for confident beginners and intermediate riders. The Dirtopia-built singletrack is flowing and well-constructed.

faqs.q: Is there coffee at Muratie?
faqs.a: Yes — Muratie has a characterful tasting room. Post-ride wine tasting at Muratie is a genuinely special experience at one of the oldest wine estates in South Africa.

faqs.q: What is the best trail at Muratie?
faqs.a: The flowing singletrack through the Simonsberg forest is the highlight. Dirtopia built these trails with care and the quality shows.

faqs.q: What is the best season for Muratie?
faqs.a: The Simonsberg slopes ride well year-round. Autumn brings vineyard colours that make the beautiful setting even more spectacular.

local_knowledge: Muratie Wine Estate is one of the oldest continuously farmed estates in South Africa, established in 1685. The tasting room feels deliberately unchanged — dark, dusty and atmospheric. Order the Ansela van de Caab red blend.

The Dirtopia trails at Muratie are maintained to a high standard. Dirtopia is one of the premier trail building companies in South Africa and their signature is smooth, bermed corners that reward momentum.
Knorhoek Road can be narrow in places. If you are parking on the road rather than in the estate car park, pull fully off the road and check visibility before opening car doors.

polkadraai.name: Polkadraai Bike Park
polkadraai.difficulty: Green: 2 trails, Blue: 2 trails, Red: 1 trail, Black: 1 trail
polkadraai.permit: Bike park only: R70. Bike park plus Bottelary Hills trails: R100. Annual options from around R400 to R700 depending on category. Buy on-site at Polkadraai Farm. No booking required, arrive, sign the indemnity and ride. Helmet compulsory, bikes must be in good condition, kids must be supervised.
polkadraai.getting_there: GPS: -33.93, 18.79. From Stellenbosch or Kuils River take Polkadraai Road (M12) and turn into Polkadraai Farm. Large dedicated parking area on-site. Easy access, well signposted, one of the most beginner-friendly setups in the region.
polkadraai.seasons: Year-round riding. Autumn and spring are the best conditions. Summer gets hot but short park sessions are manageable. The park drains well in winter and stays rideable. May close during heavy rain or lightning, check their social media before heading out.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride Polkadraai Bike Park?
faqs.a: Yes — Polkadraai has a skills zone and pump track that welcomes beginners. A great place to develop skills in a controlled environment.

faqs.q: What is at Polkadraai Bike Park?
faqs.a: Purpose-built skills zone, pump track, jump lines and connection into the Bottelary Hills Conservancy for 130km+ of XC riding.

faqs.q: Is Polkadraai good for kids?
faqs.a: Excellent. The skills zone and pump track are ideal for developing young riders safely. One of the best places in the Western Cape to introduce kids to MTB.

local_knowledge: The pump track at Polkadraai is one of the better public pump tracks in the Cape — smooth asphalt, well-shaped rollers and big enough to build real speed. Worth a dedicated session even if you do not plan to ride the XC trails.
The Polkadraai Road itself is busy with traffic, especially morning and evening commuters. Cross carefully when moving between the bike park and any roadside parking.

The Bottelary Hills connection from Polkadraai gives you access to 130km+ of XC riding, but make sure you have navigation sorted before heading into the network as the farm trails beyond the bike park are not as well-signed.

hellsend.name: Hellsend Dirt Compound
hellsend.difficulty: Red: 1 trail, Black: 4 trails, Green: 0 trails, Blue: 0 trails
hellsend.permit: No public day permit system. Access is invite-only, private sessions or event-based. DarkFest spectator tickets are around R380 and above. Exact access is coordinated privately or through event organisers, follow their Facebook and Instagram for session announcements and event dates.
hellsend.getting_there: GPS: -33.92, 18.90. Located on Helshoogte Road (R310) between Stellenbosch and Franschhoek, on Vuurberg Farm. From Stellenbosch drive up Helshoogte Pass toward Franschhoek and look for the Vuurberg Farm turn. Exact access details are shared privately or via event organisers. No public drop-in.
hellsend.seasons: Main build and event season runs December through March. Late summer, February and March, is peak season for DarkFest. Riding is highly dependent on wind, a critical factor for big jump lines, and dry conditions. Events often wait for a weather green light before proceeding.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride Hellsend Dirt Compound?
faqs.a: No. Hellsend is a private gravity playground for experienced riders only. There is no casual day permit. If you need to ask if you are ready, you are probably not ready yet.

faqs.q: How do I get access to Hellsend?
faqs.a: Hellsend is a private facility on Vuurberg Farm near Villiersdorp. Access by prior arrangement only. Contact Hellsend directly through their social channels.

faqs.q: What kind of riding is Hellsend?
faqs.a: Pure gravity. Purpose-built freeride and enduro with drops, jumps, technical lines and raw mountain terrain. This is a playground for riders who love steep and gnarly.

faqs.q: Is Hellsend worth the drive?
faqs.a: For the right rider, absolutely. Nothing else quite like it in the Western Cape.

local_knowledge: The best bit is that all riders are like-minded and there are gravity trails for days — plus lots of jumps too. It's the home of Darkfest after all.
Access is by arrangement only and sessions fill up quickly. Book well in advance, especially for weekends in the dry season from October to April when demand is highest.

Full face helmets and knee pads are strongly recommended. Hellsend is freeride territory — the features are built for experienced riders and the consequences of a fall on some of the bigger lines are significant.

paarl.name: Paarl MTB
paarl.difficulty: Green: 2 trails, Blue: 5 trails, Red: 3 trails, Black: 1 trail
paarl.permit: R100 adults, R80 kids and pensioners. One permit covers access to all trailheads across the entire Paarl Trails network, Spice Route, Laborie, Rhebokskloof, Bovenland and Fairview, sunrise to sunset. Buy online via the Paarl Trails website or from mobile vendors and trailhead sales points. No booking required.
paarl.getting_there: Multiple trailheads across Paarl. Spice Route Destination is the most popular and has the best facilities. Laborie Wine Estate, Bovenland Farm, Rhebokskloof and Fairview are all valid alternatives depending on your planned route. From Cape Town take the N1 northeast to Paarl and follow signs to your chosen trailhead. Spice Route is on the Suid Agter Paarl Road. Bovenland is quieter with more of a rider vibe. Weekends get busy so arrive early.
paarl.seasons: Autumn is the standout season, cool temperatures and tacky trails make for perfect conditions. Spring is excellent too. Summer is very hot in Paarl so start early and plan for shorter routes or carry extra water. After rain some clay sections get sticky but the network is generally still rideable. No formal closure board, check local social media for trail status.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride Paarl MTB?
faqs.a: Paarl has something for all levels. With 200km+ of trails, there are green and blue routes suitable for beginners. Start at Laborie or Spice Route for an accessible introduction.

faqs.q: How big is the Paarl MTB network?
faqs.a: 200km+ of core trails, up to 450km when you connect into surrounding wine farm trails. One of the largest MTB networks in South Africa.

faqs.q: Is there coffee at Paarl MTB?
faqs.a: Excellent options at multiple trailheads. Laborie Wine Estate and Spice Route are outstanding post-ride destinations.

faqs.q: What is the best season for Paarl MTB?
faqs.a: Paarl can be very hot in summer so start early. Autumn and spring are ideal. Winter rides are lush and green.

local_knowledge: The Paarl Trails day permit is genuinely exceptional value at R100 as it covers the entire 200km+ network across all trailheads including Spice Route, Laborie, Diamant and Bovenland to name a few.

Paarl Mountain itself is a landmark visible from most of the trail network — three enormous granite domes, each the size of a city block, sitting directly above the town. The views from the higher trails towards the mountain are dramatic.
Summer in Paarl is hot, significantly hotter than Cape Town or Stellenbosch. Plan to be off the exposed trails by 10h00 in December and January or carry double the water you think you need.

spiceroute.name: Spice Route
spiceroute.difficulty: Green: 2 trails, Blue: 4 trails, Red: 2 trails, Black: 1 trail
spiceroute.permit: R80–R100 day permit. Available online via Paarl Trails, at the trailhead info centre or via SnapScan at the start. No booking required for regular riding, only needed if you want a guided ride or bike rental.
spiceroute.getting_there: GPS: S33°45'50 E18°55'10. From Cape Town take the N1 to Paarl, then the R45 (Suid Agter Paarl Road / Franschhoek direction). Follow signs to Spice Route Destination. Safe, secure parking at the main estate lot, arrive early on weekends, it fills up fast.
spiceroute.seasons: Autumn through spring, March to November, is prime riding season. Summer gets hot so ride early mornings to beat the heat and the crowds. Trails can close after heavy rain as clay farm roads get messy and damaged. Always check trail status if it has rained recently.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride Spice Route?
faqs.a: Yes — Spice Route is one of the more accessible entry points into the Paarl Trails network.

faqs.q: What else is at Spice Route besides trails?
faqs.a: Multiple restaurants, craft beer, gin distillery, chocolate and wine. Arguably the best post-ride destination in the entire Paarl network.

faqs.q: What is the best season for Spice Route trails?
faqs.a: Year-round. Avoid peak summer heat by riding early mornings.

local_knowledge: Spice Route is also home to Doolhof Wines, Cape Brewing Company, Wilderer Distillery, Indochine restaurant and Seidelberg Chocolatier. A post-ride session here can easily become a full afternoon if you are not careful.

The trails from Spice Route connect into the wider Paarl network via marked singletrack. The first junction heading east into the network is about 2km from the farm entrance — follow the Paarl Trails signage.
The Cape Brewing Company IPA on the stoep at Spice Route after a hot Paarl ride is one of the genuinely great post-ride experiences in the Western Cape. The pizza is also excellent.

plaisir.name: Plaisir De Merle
plaisir.difficulty: Green: 1 trail, Blue: 1 trail, Red: 0 trails, Black: 0 trails
plaisir.permit: Around R100 day permit via the Banhoek Conservancy, valid for all marked MTB trails in the valley including Plaisir. Pick up at the tasting room or security gate on arrival, or via Zapper and SnapScan at the trail gate. No booking required, just carry and display your permit while riding.
plaisir.getting_there: GPS: 33°50 32S 18°57 30E. From Cape Town take the N1 to Stellenbosch, then the R45 toward Simondium and Franschhoek. Look for Plaisir de Merle signposts and estate entrance on the right. Park in the designated estate area. Trail access starts near the gate or security post. Weekends get busy so arrive early.
plaisir.seasons: Autumn through spring is best with comfortable temperatures and firmer trails. Summer is possible as some sections are shaded. The Banhoek terrain drains better than clay-heavy networks so the trail handles light rain reasonably well. Avoid riding immediately after heavy rain as the flow trail surface can soften and lose traction.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride Plaisir De Merle?
faqs.a: Yes — the Plaisir flow descent is a blue-rated trail suitable for confident beginners and intermediate riders.

faqs.q: What is the Plaisir trail like?
faqs.a: A short, fun, blue-rated flow descent with outstanding winery views. Best as part of a bigger Banhoek ride or as a standalone session.

faqs.q: Is there food and wine at Plaisir De Merle?
faqs.a: Yes — Plaisir De Merle is a prestigious wine estate with tasting facilities in the beautiful Banhoek Valley.

local_knowledge: Plaisir De Merle is a Distell-owned estate producing wines under the Plaisir de Merle label — the Grand Plaisir red blend is worth picking up at the tasting room after your ride.
The flow trail at Plaisir is directional and maintained. It drains well after rain and the berms hold up in most conditions, making it a reliable option even in the wetter months.

The Banhoek Valley light in the early morning is extraordinary — pale gold across the mountain faces and the vineyards. If you are doing a Plaisir ride as part of a Banhoek day, start here first for the best conditions.

diamante.name: Diamant Estate
diamante.difficulty: Green: 1 trail, Blue: 3 trails, Red: 2 trails, Black: 1 trail
diamante.permit: R100 day permit or R1500 annual Winelands permit. Available online via Paarl Trails, at the Specialized Paarl shop or via QR and SnapScan at the access points. No booking required for riding, only for rentals or guided rides.
diamante.getting_there: Best access is via Specialized Paarl at Bovenland Farm, most riders park there and ride in. From Cape Town take the N1 to Paarl, then the R45 (Suid Agter Paarl Road) and follow signs toward Bovenland or Specialized Paarl. Parking at Specialized is safe and secure. Diamant itself has limited direct parking.
diamante.seasons: Autumn through spring is ideal, the mountain terrain rides best when temperatures are cooler. Summer is hot and very exposed with less shade than Spice Route, so early morning starts are essential from November through March. Trails may close after rain as clay sections and jeep tracks get messy. Check the Paarl Trails network status before heading out.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride Diamant Estate?
faqs.a: Diamant is intermediate territory and requires some navigational confidence. A good destination for riders who have outgrown the easiest trails.

faqs.q: What makes Diamant special?
faqs.a: A connector zone with hidden gems that rewards exploration. A key piece of the larger Paarl Trails puzzle with some of the most interesting linking trails in the region.

local_knowledge: Diamant sits at the crossroads of several major Paarl Trails connector routes. It is hard to get a feel for the estate in isolation — plan a longer loop that uses Diamant as a waypoint rather than a destination.
The Paarl Mountain reserve boundary runs close to the Diamant trails. Stay on marked routes as the reserve has its own access and permit rules that differ from the wine farm trails.

Water sources on the Diamant connector trails are limited. The Paarl heat and the climbing on these trails mean you should carry more water than you would for an equivalent distance on flatter, cooler terrain.

montemarie.name: Monte Marie
montemarie.difficulty: Green: 1 trail, Blue: 2 trails, Red: 1 trail, Black: 0 trails
montemarie.permit: Free to ride, no permit required. Donations to the Stellenbosch Trail Fund are strongly encouraged via their website or QR codes posted at key access points on the network. If you plan to extend into private Winelands Cycling Club zones a regional permit may be needed for those sections.
montemarie.getting_there: From Cape Town take the N1 to Stellenbosch then head southwest toward Paradyskloof Road and Blaauwklippen Road. Use the Paradyskloof Pine Plantation gate or Coetzenberg Stadium parking as your trailhead. The Engen Garage on the R44 also allows you to link into trails with minimal street riding. Ride early to beat the heat and parking congestion.
montemarie.seasons: Autumn through spring is best with cooler temperatures and firmer trails. Summer is rideable but some sections are exposed so start early. After light rain the trails are generally fine. Avoid heavily saturated singletrack sections after prolonged rain as they can get muddy and slippery.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride Monte Marie?
faqs.a: Yes — Monte Marie is one of the more accessible trails in the Stellenbosch Trail Fund network. Flowing, scenic and not overly technical.

faqs.q: Is there coffee at Monte Marie?
faqs.a: Monte Marie has winery facilities. The Stellenbosch wine estate setting makes it a natural choice for a post-ride tasting or lunch.

faqs.q: What is the best trail at Monte Marie?
faqs.a: Flowing singletrack through vineyards and fynbos on the Simonsberg slopes with outstanding views across the Blaauwklippen Valley.

local_knowledge: Monte Marie sits on the Simonsberg slope above the Blaauwklippen Valley. The views across to the Hottentots Holland mountains to the east are outstanding and completely different from the Atlantic-facing views on the other side of Stellenbosch.
The Stellenbosch Trail Fund signage on the Monte Marie trails is colour coded — green, blue and red. Stick to green and blue on your first visit and save the red for when you know the network.
They have some of the best eggs Benedict you will ever experience in your life!

faircape.name: Fair Cape MTB
faircape.difficulty: Green: 1 trail, Blue: 1 trail, Red: 1 trail, Black: 0 trails
faircape.permit: R50–R60 day permit, juniors around R30. Available at the Hoogekraal farm access point, Meerendal estate, Contermanskloof and Bloemendal Trail Park, usually via honesty box or permit seller with SnapScan and Zapper available. No booking required but your permit board must be displayed on your bike. Club members get full network access including the green corridors linking the farms, non-members ride within individual farm trail boundaries.
faircape.getting_there: From Cape Town take the N1 north toward Durbanville and Bellville, then turn toward Vissershok Road. Follow signage to Hoogekraal Farm for the Faircape trail access point. Tygerberg MTB signs mark the farm entrances. Parking at the farm trailheads is secure and usually patrolled. Arrive early on weekends.
faircape.seasons: Year-round riding with autumn and spring being ideal. Summer is hot in the Durbanville hills so start early and bring plenty of water and sun protection. Green-graded trails like Faircape dry out quickly after rain. After prolonged wet weather some sections can get muddy.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride Fair Cape MTB?
faqs.a: Fair Cape is accessible to intermediate riders. The Tygerberg MTB Network spans 180km+ of XC terrain. Some navigation experience helps given the network size.

faqs.q: What is the Fair Cape MTB network like?
faqs.a: Part of one of the largest MTB networks in South Africa — spanning working farms and estates across the Durbanville Hills. Excellent for fitness-focused riding.

local_knowledge: Fair Cape Dairy is a working dairy farm. You may encounter farm vehicles, particularly in the early morning when the dairy operation is most active — keep left and move off the track when vehicles approach.

The Tygerberg MTB Club network spans multiple farms and the trail markings vary between properties. Download the Trailforks map with offline access before heading out as phone signal can be patchy in the lower-lying sections.

The Durbanville Hills network including Fair Cape is at its best from May to September when temperatures are cooler and the farm landscapes are green. Summer riding is possible but get started before 08h00.

winelands.name: Stellenzicht
winelands.difficulty: Green: 1 trail, Blue: 2 trails, Red: 1 trail, Black: 1 trail
winelands.permit: R60–R100 WLCC day permit, youth around R30–R60. Available at Stellenzicht farm permit sellers, partner bike shops and via SnapScan and Zapper at some access points. No booking required but a valid permit board tag must be displayed on your bike, it is checked. Check current pricing at the permit board on arrival as it can vary slightly by point of sale.
winelands.getting_there: Stellenzicht Wine Farm, Stellenbosch, approximately -33.9256, 18.8568. From Cape Town take the N1 toward Stellenbosch, exit into town and follow Blaauwklippen Road or the R44 toward Stellenzicht. Look for WLCC trail signage and parking near the farm gate and permit box area. Arrive early on busy weekends as parking is informal on the farm access road.
winelands.seasons: Autumn and spring are ideal with comfortable temperatures and good traction. Winter is often fine with softer ground giving good grip. Summer midday gets hot, ride early and bring extra water. After rain the elevated contour singletrack drains well but lower sections can get slick. Use your judgment and avoid deep mud after heavy rain.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride Stellenzicht?
faqs.a: Yes — Stellenzicht is one of the most beginner-friendly winery trail experiences in the Winelands. Smooth, scenic and welcoming.

faqs.q: What is Stellenzicht like to ride?
faqs.a: Country rolling singletrack weaving through vineyards and gentle hills. Relaxing, scenic and with just enough challenge to keep it interesting.

faqs.q: Is there food and wine at Stellenzicht?
faqs.a: Yes — Stellenzicht has a tasting room and restaurant.

local_knowledge: Stellenzicht produces wines in the Golden Triangle, the area between Stellenbosch, Helderberg and Franschhoek that consistently delivers some of the Cape's best red wines. The Syrah is a standout and pairs perfectly with a post-ride platter.
The Helderberg slopes where Stellenzicht sits enjoy a different microclimate from the Cape Flats. Afternoon cloud often builds over the mountains while the vineyard trails below stay in sunshine.

The rolling vineyard singletrack at Stellenzicht is ideal for introducing friends to MTB. Manageable climbs, clear signage and a winery at the finish make it a reliable choice for mixed-ability groups.

greyton.name: Greyton MTB
greyton.difficulty: Green: 2 trails, Blue: 3 trails, Red: 2 trails, Black: 1 trail
greyton.permit: R75 day permit, R120 weekend, R800 annual single, R1250 annual family. Buy at 41 Main Road in Greyton or via the Hub and Spoke MTB Cafe. Pay by EFT, SnapScan, card or cash and submit your details online. Display your permit board on your handlebars while riding. No advance booking needed.
greyton.getting_there: GPS: -34.0515, 19.6075. From Cape Town take the N2 east toward Caledon, then turn onto the R406 toward Greyton and follow signs into the village. The trailhead is right in town. Park on the street or in designated trailhead parking areas near the trail start and the cafes. Arrive early on weekends in peak season as village parking fills up.
greyton.seasons: Autumn and spring are ideal with mild temperatures and good trail conditions. Summer gets hot, start early and carry plenty of water. After rain some dirt singletrack can get slick and slow. There is no formal closure system so check local Facebook groups or the Hub and Spoke Cafe for current conditions if it has rained.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride Greyton MTB?
faqs.a: Greyton has options for all levels. Less technically demanding than the mountain trails near Cape Town, making it accessible to motivated beginners.

faqs.q: Is Greyton worth the drive from Cape Town?
faqs.a: Absolutely. A hidden gem of Western Cape MTB. Stay overnight and make the most of it — the village is charming and the Overberg landscape feels completely different.

faqs.q: Is there coffee at Greyton?
faqs.a: Yes — Greyton village has excellent cafes and restaurants. The food scene is outstanding and the whole village is geared towards visitors.

local_knowledge: Greyton village has a strict aesthetic. The historical conservation area rules mean the town looks largely unchanged from decades ago — this is part of the charm. Park near the main square and walk to the trailhead rather than trying to drive.
The Oak and Vigne Bistro on Main Road is the best post-ride food in town. Sourdough, local produce and excellent coffee. Get there before 11h00 on weekends as it fills fast.

The Greyton to McGregor trail is a well-known day hike but the MTB crossing is more challenging and requires good navigation skills. If you plan to cross into McGregor by bike, go with someone who has done it before.

george.name: Witfontein George
george.difficulty: Green: 2 trails, Blue: 3 trails, Red: 2 trails, Black: 1 trail
george.permit: Free self-issue permits at the Cape Nature office at the trailhead. Fill in your details and carry the permit with you while riding. Permits are not sold online, take one at the office even after hours. No advance booking required. Note that some sections can be affected by forestry harvesting or maintenance so check local notice boards or the George Trails website before heading out.
george.getting_there: GPS: -33.9465, 22.4651. From George town centre head northwest on Outeniqua Road or the R328 and follow signs toward the Cape Nature office and Witfontein plantation area. Parking is available at trailheads near the office and at the Botanical Gardens which opens access to more contour loops. Arrive early on weekends as some areas fill up.
george.seasons: Year-round riding with autumn and spring being most pleasant. Winter rains can make some forest roads slippery and the sandy loamy soil holds water after heavy rain, check local reports before heading out. Sections can occasionally be restricted due to forestry operations so check the George Trails site or local trail notice boards for current conditions.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride Witfontein George?
faqs.a: Witfontein has options for most levels. Pine plantation and jeep track sections suit beginners while contour singletrack offers more challenge.

faqs.q: How much is the George trails permit?
faqs.a: Witfontein operates a self-issue permit system — free to ride. Contributions are appreciated and support trail maintenance.

faqs.q: Is Witfontein worth making a trip for?
faqs.a: Yes — especially if heading to the Garden Route. George and the Outeniqua network offer a completely different riding experience to the Cape.

local_knowledge: The Witfontein permit system is an honesty box. There is a small tin at the trailhead for voluntary contributions — the trail fund runs on goodwill and volunteer labour, so contribute what you can.

George gets significantly more rain than Cape Town. The Outeniqua mountains wring moisture from the Indian Ocean weather systems year-round. Check conditions before heading to Witfontein and expect the trails to be damper than equivalent Cape trails.

The Garden Route MTB community is tight-knit and welcoming. If you are visiting from Cape Town, ask in the George MTB Facebook group for current conditions and local trail tips before you drive four and a half hours.

laborie.name: Laborie Wine Estate
laborie.difficulty: Blue: 2 trails, Red: 2 trails, Black: 1 trail, Green: 0 trails
laborie.permit: R100 adults, R80 kids and pensioners. One day permit gives full access to the entire Paarl Trails network including Laborie, Spice Route, Rhebokskloof and Bovenland. Buy online via the Paarl Trails website before you arrive or via SnapScan and payment boards at trailhead access points. No booking required, just carry or display your permit. Annual and Wine Lands Regional permits also available for frequent riders.
laborie.getting_there: GPS: -33.7515, 18.9645. From Cape Town take the N1 northeast toward Paarl, exit at Paarl and follow signs toward Laborie Estate on Taillefer Street or Main Road, Suider Paarl. Parking is available at the estate close to the trailhead. Arrive early on weekends as it gets busy.
laborie.seasons: Autumn and spring are ideal with mild weather and good conditions. Summer heat in Paarl can be intense, start early and bring plenty of water. Winter brings more moisture and some sections can get slippery. Check social media or trail status before heading out after rain.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride Laborie Wine Estate?
faqs.a: Yes — Laborie is an accessible starting point for the Paarl Trails network with beginner-friendly options.

faqs.q: What makes Laborie a good base?
faqs.a: Laborie sits at the entry point to 200km+ of Paarl Trails with excellent on-site facilities and Paarl town immediately nearby.

faqs.q: Is there food and wine at Laborie?
faqs.a: Yes — Laborie has an excellent restaurant and wine tasting. The Paarl Brewery is also nearby.

local_knowledge: Laborie is literally on the edge of Paarl town. You can walk from the estate to the main street in five minutes, making it the most accessible entry point to the Paarl Trails network for visitors staying in town.
The Laborie restaurant is a KWV property and the wine list is extensive. The estate produces a good method cap classique sparkling wine that is worth a try post-ride if the budget allows.

Paarl Mountain looms directly above the Laborie trails. The granite domes are visible from most of the estate and the scale of them is genuinely imposing up close. The trails in the reserve above require a separate SANParks permit.

uitsig.name: Constantia Uitsig Bike Park
uitsig.difficulty: Green: 2 trails, Blue: 2 trails, Red: 1 trail, Black: 1 trail
uitsig.permit: Entry fee approximately R50 to R80 per rider, paid on arrival at the estate. No booking required for casual riding. Group bookings can be arranged with the estate. Helmet compulsory.
uitsig.getting_there: GPS: -34.047509, 18.423595. From Cape Town CBD take Constantia Main Road and turn into Constantia Uitsig Wine Estate. Follow signs to the bike park. On-site parking, secure and easy for families.
uitsig.seasons: Year-round riding. Spring and autumn are the most pleasant. The pump track and dirt jump lines can get soft after heavy rain so check conditions before heading out. Trails are well maintained and drain reasonably well.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride Constantia Uitsig Bike Park?
faqs.a: Yes — one of the best beginner and family MTB destinations in Cape Town. Purpose-built for developing riders from scratch in a safe, beautiful setting.

faqs.q: Is Constantia Uitsig good for kids?
faqs.a: Excellent. The skills park is designed to develop young riders progressively. One of the best family MTB destinations in Cape Town.

faqs.q: Is there coffee at Constantia Uitsig?
faqs.a: Yes — Constantia Uitsig is a wine estate with a restaurant. The Constantia Valley has some of Cape Town's best dining and coffee immediately nearby.

faqs.q: Does Constantia Uitsig link to other trails?
faqs.a: Yes — the bike park connects into the Constantia Greenbelt trails for riders wanting to extend their ride.

local_knowledge: The estate car park is available for trail users but it does get full. They now have a ticket and boom system so make sure your preferred payment method is accepted.

The skills park progression is well thought out. Start on the smallest features and work your way up rather than jumping straight to the jump lines — the berms on the flow trail are beginner-friendly and a great place to build confidence.

The Greenbelt connection from Constantia Uitsig opens up the entire Constantia Valley trail network. Experienced riders can link through to Tokai Forest, Cecilia and beyond for a full morning of varied riding.

boschendal.name: Boschendal Wine Estate
boschendal.difficulty: Green: 2 trails, Blue: 2 trails, Red: 1 trail, Black: 2 trails
boschendal.permit: R115 day permit per rider (R95 for pensioners). Trail Run and Hiking permit R95. In-house guests ride complimentary. Available from the Trail Centre at the Boschendal Werf. Open Monday to Sunday 08h00 to 17h00. Trail opening times are weather dependent and rentals are subject to availability. Note: MTB trail rates exclude bike and helmet rental. 100% of permit fees go toward building, maintaining and alien clearing on the trails. Winelands Regional Permit also covers Boschendal. No permit, no ride. Bike hire available on site — contact trailcentre@boschendal.co.za or call +27 (021) 870 4238.
boschendal.getting_there: GPS: -33.871, 18.972. Boschendal Wine Estate, R310 Pniel Road, Groot Drakenstein, Franschhoek 7680. Take the R310 over Helshoogte Pass from Stellenbosch toward Franschhoek. Park at the main Boschendal Werf parking area — secure, with toilets and shower facilities. From the parking area it is a short 1km ride to the trail start just inside the Rhodes Avenue security gate on the other side of the R310.
boschendal.seasons: Open 365 days a year. Autumn is spectacular with incredible vine colours across the estate. Spring is lush and the views of the mountains are stunning. Summer can be hot on the exposed climbs so start early, before 08h00 if possible. Trails are weather dependent and the Trail Centre will advise on closures. After rain some sections can get muddy but the trails generally drain well.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride Boschendal Wine Estate?
faqs.a: Boschendal has trails for all levels with five colour-coded circuits from 4km to 23km. The green and shorter blue routes are suitable for beginners. The world-class facilities make it a great destination regardless of your level.

faqs.q: How much is the Boschendal permit?
faqs.a: R115 day permit per rider (R95 for pensioners). Trail run and hiking permit R95. Open Monday to Sunday 08h00 to 17h00. In-house guests ride complimentary. Contact trailcentre@boschendal.co.za or call +27 (021) 870 4238.

faqs.q: Where do I park at Boschendal?
faqs.a: GPS: -33.871, 18.972. R310 Pniel Road, Groot Drakenstein. Take Helshoogte Pass from Stellenbosch. Park at the main Boschendal Werf — secure with toilets and showers.

faqs.q: What are the best descents at Boschendal?
faqs.a: The three signature descents are Inferno (3.7km), Sugar Bowl (2.3km) and Porcupine (1.3km). Each is exceptional.

faqs.q: Is there food at Boschendal after riding?
faqs.a: Exceptional. The Boschendal Deli is world-class, the Farm Shop is stocked with fresh produce and picnics on the lawns are available. One of the most beautiful places to spend a morning in the Western Cape.

faqs.q: Can I hire a bike at Boschendal?
faqs.a: Yes — bike hire including e-bikes is available at the Trail Centre. Contact trailcentre@boschendal.co.za to arrange in advance.

faqs.q: What is the Winelands Regional Permit?
faqs.a: The Winelands Regional Permit covers Boschendal alongside Banhoek, Paarl Trails, Franschhoek and Wellington trails. Worth it if you plan to ride multiple winery hubs.

local_knowledge: The Boschendal Deli picnic is one of the great Western Cape experiences. Big wicker baskets of local produce eaten on the lawns under the oak trees — book well in advance for weekends as it sells out regularly.

The Helshoogte Pass approach from Stellenbosch is the most scenic way to arrive. The road winds through mountain fynbos with the Groot Drakenstein mountains ahead of you — build in 10 extra minutes just to enjoy the drive.

In-house guests at Boschendal ride complimentary. If you are making a weekend of it, staying on the estate means you can be on the trails before other day visitors arrive — the Inferno descent in the early morning with no one else on it is something special.

arc.name: ARC of Franschhoek
arc.difficulty: Blue: 2 trails, Red: 2 trails, Black: 1 trail
arc.permit: Day and annual passes available via Quicket (search "The ARC of Franschhoek Pass"). Prices include VAT, booking fee not included. Kids under 8 and guests with disabilities enjoy free access. Annual passes are valid for the calendar year. 100% of pass fees go toward ecological restoration, local employment and building a regenerative trail network in partnership with the SA Trails Network NPC.
arc.getting_there: GPS: -33.9337821, 19.0812915. Berg River Dam, Robertsvlei, near Franschhoek. From Franschhoek village follow the Robertsvlei Road out towards the dam — the ARC Club and parking are clearly marked. Allow extra time on the gravel approach road.
arc.seasons: Every season offers something different. Cooler months are fantastic for riding, especially when the fynbos is green and the air is crisp. After rain the landscape turns spectacular with the colours coming alive. Spring is particularly special as the fynbos begins to flower and the whole landscape changes. Respect temporary closures when conditions are too wet or sensitive — this is an actively rehabilitating landscape.

faqs.q: Can beginners ride at ARC of Franschhoek?
faqs.a: ARC suits intermediate riders best. There is serious climbing on most routes and Dam360 and Snake Alley both demand fitness and skill. Confident beginners can enjoy the shorter valley sections near the ARC Club but the bigger loops are not a first-timer destination.

faqs.q: How much is the ARC of Franschhoek pass?
faqs.a: Day and annual passes are available via Quicket — search 'The ARC of Franschhoek Pass'. Kids under 8 and guests with disabilities ride free. Annual passes run for the calendar year. 100 percent of pass fees go towards ecological restoration and trail building.

faqs.q: Where do I park at ARC of Franschhoek?
faqs.a: Park at the ARC Club above the Berg River Dam in Robertsvlei, just outside Franschhoek. GPS -33.9337821, 19.0812915. The approach road has a gravel section so allow extra time.

faqs.q: Which trail should I ride first at ARC of Franschhoek?
faqs.a: Start at the ARC Club and take the path on the left of the Sunset Boma down into the valley past the old pump house. Cross the river, take in the weir at the Riverstone picnic spot, then climb the paved road before it turns to gravel and drops into Flight of the Fish Eagle down to the Wolvekloof River. Return via the Wolvekloof Contour gravel road. If you have time, Snake Alley's turnoff is on the right just before the jeep track turns back to paved.

faqs.q: Is there coffee at ARC of Franschhoek?
faqs.a: Yes — the on-site coffee spot usually opens around 08h30. It's run by someone who cycles in from the village each morning, so it's worth timing your ride to make the most of it.

faqs.q: What is Dam360 at ARC of Franschhoek?
faqs.a: Dam360 is the network's signature trail — 20km with the best views of the entire Berg River Dam and surrounding landscape, roughly 2.5 hours by MTB. It captures the whole vision of the ARC project: moving through a landscape that is being actively restored rather than just riding from A to B.

faqs.q: What is the best season to ride ARC of Franschhoek?
faqs.a: Every season offers something different. Cooler months are excellent when the fynbos is green and the air is crisp. After rain the colours come alive. Spring is especially good as the fynbos flowers and transforms the whole landscape. Always respect temporary closures during wet or sensitive conditions.

faqs.q: Where should I stay near ARC of Franschhoek?
faqs.a: Franschhoek village is about 20 minutes away with excellent accommodation and dining options for making a full weekend of it.

local_knowledge: Coffee at the ARC Club opens around 08h30 — the barista cycles in from the village each morning, so don't rush there at 07h00 expecting it to be open.

From the ARC Club, take the path on the left of the Sunset Boma down to the valley past the old pump house, cross the river at the weir near the Riverstone picnic spot, then climb the paved road before it turns to gravel into Flight of the Fish Eagle down to the Wolvekloof River — return via the Wolvekloof Contour.
If you've got the legs and time, Snake Alley's turnoff is on the right just before the jeep track turns back to paved road — worth the detour for experienced riders.
